S1P7-U11-WELDED-TOKEN.what: S1.13.7.12.6 [class-1 re-audit 4 U11, major] - check-finding-guards asked whether a guard token was on ONE PHYSICAL LINE. A guard token is a sentence, and a sentence is the most wrappable thing in this repo. Measured on S1P1-B1-OWNER: Prettier's ordinary output for its assertion left the assertion intact and the gate said 'the guard is gone', 267 -> 266 guarded, in the instrument that decides whether every finding in the audit is closed, with MAX_UNGUARDED capped at 1 and no allow-list. ONE PRODUCER now: lib/joinedCode, merging unreadInputsCopy's junction welds with this gate's block-comment tracking; the RN test's local copy is DELETED rather than parked. Two defects found while building it, both by measurement: for...of walks code POINTS while regex indices are code UNITS, so one emoji desynchronised lineAt and the welds ate real characters; and normalising the haystack without the needle cost 8 guards outright (268 -> 260) because registry tokens carry their own indentation on purpose. >>> THE GUARD'S UN-FIX REVERTS THE FIRST PRESENCE CHECK, NOT presentInCode, AND THE REASON IS CIRCULARITY: this entry's own token is the line inside presentInCode, so reverting THAT makes lint:finding-guards red by reporting this very guard missing - a tautology wearing a measurement's clothes, and the harness scored it FAULT-BASELINE-ALREADY-RED. Reverting the first presence check instead leaves the gate GREEN on a clean tree (measured), so the wrap-escapes recipe can actually reach its verdict: a wrapped guard token then fails there and the gate refuses correct code. >>> AND THE RUN IS lint:finding-guards, NOT test:wrap-escapes, for a SECOND circularity: an un-fix REPLACES its own anchor line, and this gate validates that every proof's anchor still matches exactly once - so routing the proof through a chain containing this gate makes its baseline red for a reason that is about the harness rather than the defect (measured: FAULT-BASELINE-ALREADY-RED, twice). The un-fix is therefore TWO edits - revert the weld AND wrap a real guard token - and the expected string names the file whose guard is falsely reported missing, which a green run cannot print. Measured: the wrap ALONE, with the fix intact, leaves the gate green at 268. >>> THIRD circularity, and the fix is to SPLIT them: the guard pins ONE call site (the first presence check) and its un-fix reverts the OTHER (presentInCode), so neither the registry anchor nor the wrap-escapes recipe's control sits on the line the other needs intact. Anchoring both on one line made every attempt to observe the gate without the fix red for `anchor matches 0x` - a complaint about the harness wearing a measurement's clothes, measured three times.
